Going right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,5). So the line goes up.
Going up leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes around the edge to (6,1).
Going right would leave number 7 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going around the edge to (1,1), the next 5 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,6). So the line goes up.

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going around the edge to (6,2) would leave number 10 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 10. So the line goes right.
Number 10 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (2,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going down would leave number 12 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
The line must go right: down is number 13, which comes later.
Going down would strand number 12: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
